text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Both tax reductions and subsidies to entrepreneurs will be used in experimental support for households for buying services.
- Finns' optimism has returned but they are unsatisfied with the dominance of market economy, a survey by the Centre for Finnish Business and Policy Studies (EVA) shows.
- More Finns die falling over in slippery weather than in traffic: 800 versus 400. @
- NATO membership may one day become topical for Finland but is not now, said Gustav Hagglund, commander of the Finnish army, visiting the U.S.
- More reindeer are starving to death in Lapland due to thick and exceptionally icy snow.
- Helsinki University hospital to raise its alertness for Yeltsin-Clinton summit on March 20 to 21.
- One in 10 Finnish schools have sponsorhip agreements with businesses.
- One third of Finnish students live on less than 1,000 markka a month, report shows. @
- Strict anti-drugs policy or a softer approach to cannabis divides City of Helsinki officials into two camps.
- Energy consumption to grow less than the economy as a whole as services take over from industry, ministry of trade and industry report says.
- Finland's total assets are worth some 2,200 billion markka, which is about 1.1 million per houshold. Each of the eight wealthiest companies in the world have more. @
KAUPPALEHTI

- Former Kansallis-Osake-Pankki director Peter Fagernas who left the bank when it merged to form Merita has converted his fund managing company Conventum into an investment bank, after it failed to raise enough capital.
- Competition authority examining how to boost competition in public transport in Helsinki and Turku. Competition may lower prices by 10 to 30 percent.
- Import restrictions helped state monopoly Alko's 1996 profit to the same level as in 1995. @
- Some 50 companies to join Finland Exports' campaign in St Petersburg.
AAMULEHTI
- Finns and Portuguese are the least informed about the European Union, EU survey shows.
DEMARI
- Erkki Tuomioja, chairman of the Social Democratic Party's parliamentary group, says it may take up to eight years before EU accepts new members. @
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Ice breakers are assisting ships stuck in consolidated ice in the eastern Gulf of Finland.
